small_guidance:
- The current kernel reloads the full weight matrix (N×K = 32768×32768 = 4GB) per row of x — this is the dominant cost. Switch the loop order: outer loop over K-tiles, inner loop over N-tiles, so x is loaded once per row but more importantly use `tl.dot` with a 2D tile of x (BLOCK_M rows at a time) to amortize weight loads across rows.
- Use a proper 2D GEMM tiling: BLOCK_M=32 or 64 (covers all 128 rows in 2-4 programs), BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32-64, with `tl.dot` instead of `tl.sum(w * x[None,:])`. This will give ~10x throughput on the matmul itself.
- Add autotune configs sweeping (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) ∈ {(32,128,32),(64,128,32),(32,256,32),(64,64,64)} with num_warps 4/8, num_stages 3-4 to overlap K-loop loads.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a two-stage fused GEMM+reduce: stage 1 is a tiled GEMM with `tl.dot` over (M=128, N=32768, K=32768) producing per-tile partial sums of sigmoid(x@W^T + b) reduced along N; stage 2 (or atomic-add into out[m]) finalizes the row sum. Grid = (cdiv(M, BLOCK_M), cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)); each program computes a BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N tile via tl.dot, applies bias+sigmoid in the epilogue, reduces along N within the tile, and atomic-adds into out[m_block].
- Ensure W is pre-transposed (or load it with the K axis contiguous via W.t().contiguous()) so the inner GEMM load is coalesced; the current `stride_wk=1` load pattern works but pair it with `tl.dot` semantics (B should have K as the contiguous reduction axis).
- With M=128 only, consider a persistent kernel where each program handles the full N-sweep for a single (or few) row(s), keeping x[m,:] tiles staged in shared memory across the N-loop — but only viable once the inner loop uses tl.dot. Use BLOCK_M=128 in one program-Y and split N across programs with atomic-add reduction into out.
